rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with its only loss a road stumble at Cincinnati, and wins over Houston, Arizona, Arizona State and Oklahoma State give it the Big 12's strongest full resume alongside Utah.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road or neutral wins, including a 49-7 rout of SMU and a road win over Louisville, though its schedule strength is the softest among the one-loss teams.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU, and both losses were one-score games to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's two losses are one-score games to Georgia and Tennessee, offset by wins over LSU, Florida State, Texas A&M, South Carolina and Vanderbilt.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's 9-2 mark includes a home win over Alabama and wins at Georgia Tech, Arkansas and Texas A&M, with narrow losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.BYU: BYU's 9-2 resume features a home win over Notre Dame plus wins over Arizona, Iowa State and Kansas State, tempered by losses to Utah and UCF.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a home win over USC and road wins at Michigan and Nebraska, and both losses — Ohio State and Washington — were by a combined five points.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 9-2 with road wins at Michigan, Washington, Illinois and Northwestern, and its only losses came to Ohio State and a one-point game at Minnesota.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia owns the best collection of direct results, beating Alabama on the road, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri, Florida and South Carolina; the lone Auburn loss is outweighed by that stacked head-to-head ledger.
rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten and its direct wins over BYU, Houston and Arizona carry the day among comparable resumes, with the Arizona road escape the tiebreak over BYU's loss.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's road loss at BYU is close, but its head-to-head home win over Miami plus a dominant 10-1 FBS mark edges the Hurricanes in a near-equal resume.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss is the direct game at Notre Dame, so despite strong wins at Wake Forest and Clemson the Hurricanes sit behind the Irish and ahead of Texas.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU, but the head-to-head neutral loss to Oklahoma and home loss to Florida cap the Longhorns below Miami.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 in FBS with direct wins over Houston and Arizona, giving the Red Raiders the head-to-head edge over Alabama's two-loss SEC profile.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's wins over Kentucky, South Carolina and LSU are solid, but the direct losses to Georgia and Tennessee outweigh the broader SEC schedule strength.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama head-to-head and owns wins over LSU and Auburn, but the direct home loss to Texas and road loss at South Carolina keep the Vols behind the Tide.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest's only loss is the direct game to Miami, but its road win at Louisville and blowout wins over SMU, NC State and Georgia Tech make a strong 10-1 case.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with the decisive road head-to-head win at Oregon and a narrow loss at Michigan; the direct result over the Ducks drives this placement.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame and Arizona head-to-head but the road loss at Utah and the UCF defeat leave the Cougars behind the Utes among Big 12 contenders.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's home loss to Ohio State is close, but the head-to-head win over USC and road wins at Nebraska and Michigan support a top-12 case.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia passes every visual test with a +23.9 FBS scoring margin and emphatic road blowouts over Alabama, Ole Miss, and South Carolina.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains unblemished at 11-0, pairing a smothering defense with gutty ranked victories over BYU, Arizona, and Houston.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame looks the part of a complete titan, boasting a +25.3 margin and an imposing 31-24 victory over Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami has steamrolled competition with an explosive offense and four road wins, their only blemish coming in a hard-fought contest in South Bend.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech passes the eye test with dynamic offensive firepower, a 10-1 record, and decisive head-to-head triumphs over Arizona and Houston.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA features an overpowering defense allowing them to control games cleanly, underscored by a pivotal road victory over Oregon.
rationales.Texas: Texas possesses exceptional raw speed and big wins over Tennessee and Ohio State, though minor execution lapses led to two tight setbacks.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest looks like a well-oiled machine, destroying ACC competition by an average margin of 23.3 points per game.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama controls games at the line of scrimmage, though a pair of tough SEC road tests cracked their armor.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee displays a lethal offense and dominant defensive front, highlighted by a commanding 26-10 win over Alabama.
rationales.BYU: BYU looks tough and physical in every phase, holding a marquee victory over Notre Dame while losing only to unbeaten Utah and UCF.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana showcases a disciplined, stingy team identity that dismantled Rutgers and USC, with their only losses coming in one-score dogfights.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's margins of 27-8 at a neutral site over Florida, 42-7 at Ole Miss, and 48-21 over Missouri show dominance, with the lone loss a 24-27 home defeat to Auburn.
rationales.Miami: Miami has won 9 of 10 with a 24-point average margin and a 31-24 home win over Notre Dame, the only ranked-opponent loss on the packet's list.
rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten, and its close 40-39 win at Arizona and 28-20 win over BYU show how it closes out tight games.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record includes a 31-24 home loss to Miami, but a 58-7 Stanford win and a 41-7 win over Boston College show strong margins.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 17-20 home loss to Georgia is its only blemish against a strong opponent, but wins over Florida State 50-36 and LSU 31-13 show strength.
rationales.Texas: Texas has four one-score wins against a schedule that includes Ohio State, Ole Miss, and LSU, but losses to Florida and Oklahoma came by three points.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's 26-10 home win over Alabama and 34-6 win over Kentucky show the offensive punch, offset by a 24-27 home loss to South Carolina.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State has big early wins, but close losses to Oregon 28-41 and USC 18-30 and a one-score home loss to Indiana temper its profile.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana won 13 of its games by a 13.6 average margin, beating Ohio State 19-15 on the road while losing to Washington 24-27.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech won 9 of 10, including road wins at Oklahoma State 52-27 and Arizona State 53-25, and a home win over Arizona 34-26.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa won at Michigan 20-19 and beat Washington 41-24 on the road, but a 14-31 home loss to Ohio State and a 10-13 loss to Minnesota hurt.
rationales.BYU: BYU has a home win over Notre Dame 28-24 and Arizona 28-17 but lost 20-28 at Utah and 31-39 at UCF.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays atop the AP order at 9-1, with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri offsetting only the home loss to Auburn.
rationales.Utah: Undefeated Utah retains second on its 10-0 FBS record and wins over BYU, Arizona and Houston, including the decisive late-season head-to-head results.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame remains third after beating Miami and SMU convincingly, though BYU's earlier win over the Irish keeps its case from being spotless.
rationales.Miami: Miami's 9-1 record and wins over Wake Forest, Clemson and Florida State support fourth, while Notre Dame's head-to-head win is its lone defeat.
rationales.Texas: Texas keeps fifth after a strong 9-2 slate, with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss and Missouri and a narrow loss to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon rises from AP 14 after beating Ohio State and Michigan on the road; its 7-3 record and losses to UCLA, Illinois and Oklahoma State temper the move.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 mark includes wins over USC, Michigan and Nebraska; its late loss to Washington and home defeat by Ohio State hold it below the top six.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech stays in the upper tier at 9-1, with wins over Houston, Arizona and Oklahoma State, but its loss to Cincinnati and less imposing schedule keep it outside the top seven.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's wins over Alabama and LSU bolster its 8-2 resume, while the Texas and South Carolina losses prevent a larger rise.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 8-2 record and wins over LSU, Texas A&M and Florida State remain impressive, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee keep it behind the stronger one-loss teams.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's 10-1 record and road win over Oregon are excellent, but its schedule strength and narrow loss at Michigan leave it just outside the top ten.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest's 9-1 record and broad road success stand out, but the home loss to Miami and softer schedule context place it behind UCLA.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays No. 1: 10-1 with the lone blemish a one-point Auburn loss, plus wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri and Florida by a 23.9 average margin.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with five road/neutral wins, beating BYU, Houston, Arizona, Iowa State and TCU without a loss all season.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's only loss is a one-score road game at BYU, and it avenged nothing needed by beating Miami and routing SMU, Stanford, Navy and Boston College.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with the sole loss a one-point road defeat at Notre Dame, including wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Florida State and Pittsburgh.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with two one-score losses (Oklahoma, Florida) but elite wins over Ohio State, LSU, Ole Miss, Missouri and Tennessee.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 9-2 with two losses to the SEC's top two (Georgia, Tennessee) and a resume featuring LSU, Florida State, Texas A&M and South Carolina wins.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with close losses to Texas and South Carolina, offset by a dominant home win over Alabama and road wins at Arkansas and Texas A&M.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with its only loss to Miami, a 23.3 average margin and six road/neutral wins including SMU, Louisville and Georgia Tech.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1, its lone loss a road upset at Cincinnati, with wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Arizona State.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with one-score losses to Utah and UCF but a signature home win over Notre Dame plus Arizona, Iowa State and Kansas.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with one-score losses to Ohio State and Washington, and the USC win keeps it ahead of other two-loss contenders despite the new Washington defeat.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 8-3 but with the best wins of any three-loss team: Ohio State, USC and Boise State, and it closed by hammering Michigan State 45-7.

rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten at 10-0 against FBS opponents, with wins over BYU, Arizona, and Houston and no losses.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia’s 9-1 FBS record includes wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, and Missouri; its only loss is a narrow home defeat to Auburn.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame’s 10-1 mark and wins over Miami, SMU, and Wisconsin outweigh its four-point road loss to BYU.
rationales.Texas: Texas owns wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, and its two losses were both by three points; its 9-2 record earns the close comparison with Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami’s 9-1 record features wins over Clemson, Wake Forest, and Florida State, with its only loss coming at Notre Dame.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana has beaten USC, Michigan, and Nebraska and its only two defeats were by four and three points, respectively.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon’s wins at Ohio State and USC and over Boise State are strong, though losses to UCLA, Illinois, and Oklahoma State temper its 7-3 FBS record.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with wins over Arizona and Houston and a road loss to Cincinnati; its strong record puts it ahead of comparable resumes.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee’s wins over Alabama and LSU support its 8-2 record, despite losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama has an 8-2 FBS record and notable wins at LSU and over Texas A&M, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee hold it below the top tier.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest’s 9-1 record includes a road win over Louisville and a decisive win at SMU, while Miami handed it its lone loss.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 and owns a road win over Oregon, but its schedule-strength proxy is less compelling than the teams above it.

rationales.Utah: Utah is 10-0 against FBS teams, has no losses, and pairs a 21.7 SP+ with wins over BYU, Houston, Arizona, Cincinnati, and Iowa State.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia’s 9-1 FBS record, 31.3 SP+, 28.675 FPI, and wins over Alabama, Ole Miss, and Oklahoma outweigh its lone loss to Auburn.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with a 24.4 SP+ and 24.282 FPI; its only loss is to Notre Dame, and its wins include Wake Forest and Clemson.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame’s 10-1 record, 25.6 SP+, 27.212 FPI, and head-to-head win over Miami support a place ahead of the Hurricanes despite the BYU loss.
rationales.Texas: Texas has a 22.4 SP+ and 25.373 FPI, plus wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, though its losses to Oklahoma and Florida temper the case.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana’s 23.1 SP+ leads this group, and wins over USC, Nebraska, Michigan, and Northwestern strengthen its 8-2 FBS resume despite losses to Ohio State and Washington.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon’s 18.3 SP+ and 21.349 FPI accompany wins over Ohio State, USC, Boise State, and Michigan, but its three losses include UCLA and Illinois.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 and rates 21.1 in SP+, with a road win over Oregon; its only loss is a narrow road defeat at Michigan.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama’s 22.9 SP+ and 24.21 FPI support its 8-2 record and wins over LSU, Texas A&M, and Florida State, although it lost to both Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with a 19.4 SP+ and wins over Houston and Arizona, while its only loss came on the road against Cincinnati.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee’s 8-2 mark and 21.5 SP+ include wins over Alabama, LSU, and Kentucky, balanced by losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest has a 22.6 SP+ and 9-1 FBS record, but its 0.43 schedule proxy and loss to Miami limit a resume with Louisville as its strongest listed win.

rationales.Texas: Texas has the strongest blend of SP+ (22.4) and FPI (25.4) among the group, with a 9-2 record, three ranked wins, and a road win over Tennessee, though its losses to Oklahoma and Florida are real.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with SP+ 21.7 and FPI 19.4, its only ranked wins (BYU, Houston, Arizona) came away from a schedule with a 0.48 FBS SOS proxy, and it has no losses.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia has the best FPI in the packet (28.7) and SP+ (31.3), with a 9-1 FBS record, a 23.9 mean FBS margin, and wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, and Florida.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with SP+ 24.4, FPI 24.3, a 0.57 FBS SOS proxy, and an 18.1 mean FBS margin; its lone loss is a road defeat to Notre Dame, which it beat head to head in the Miami-Notre Dame matchup only once.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with SP+ 25.6, FPI 27.2, and the highest mean FBS margin in the packet (25.3), but its SOS proxy (0.46) and loss to BYU keep it below Miami.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama has SP+ 22.9 and FPI 24.2 with a 9-2 record and a 16.9 mean margin, but two losses (Georgia, Tennessee) and a 0.53 SOS proxy keep it below the top tier.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon has SP+ 18.3, FPI 21.3, a 0.61 SOS proxy (highest among the top 10), and a 10-1 road-heavy resume with wins over USC and Ohio State.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State has SP+ 24.1 and FPI 23.2 with a 0.56 SOS proxy, but a 7-4 record including a loss to Oregon and a 15-19 home loss to Indiana.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with SP+ 22.6, FPI 20.2, a 23.3 mean margin, and a 0.43 SOS proxy, with its only loss to Miami; the schedule context is weaker than the efficiency.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with SP+ 18.0 and FPI 15.3, a 0.54 SOS proxy, and wins over Notre Dame and Arizona, but two losses (Utah, UCF) cap it.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with SP+ 19.4 and FPI 17.1, its only loss to Cincinnati; its wins over Houston, Arizona, and Oklahoma State are solid but its SOS proxy (0.47) is middling.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with SP+ 21.1 and FPI 12.6, a 16.5 mean margin, and a road win over Oregon, but its FPI is far below the top tier.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia holds the top spot with a dominant resume highlighted by a 20-17 road victory over Alabama.
rationales.Utah: Undefeated Utah earns the second seed backed by decisive head-to-head wins over both BYU and Houston.
rationales.Texas: Texas secures the third seed featuring head-to-head victories over Tennessee and Ohio State alongside nine FBS wins.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame claims the fourth spot, driven by an elite body of work and a 31-24 victory over Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami slots behind Notre Dame due to that direct loss but remains top five with a 33-20 head-to-head win over Wake Forest.
rationales.BYU: BYU ranks sixth by virtue of their 28-24 direct head-to-head victory over Notre Dame and a win over Arizona.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech takes seventh behind a sterling 10-1 record with direct wins over Houston and Arizona.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama places eighth, having lost directly to Georgia and Tennessee while defeating Kentucky and South Carolina.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee sits behind Texas due to their 20-17 head-to-head loss but ahead of Alabama thanks to a 26-10 direct victory.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA enters the top ten at 10-1, highlighted by their direct 17-15 head-to-head victory over Oregon.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest stands at 10-1 with an impressive road win over Louisville, sitting just behind the elite one-loss teams.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana captures the final playoff spot at 9-2 on the strength of a 27-13 head-to-head win over USC.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia owns the packet's best win set, beating Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina, with only a 24-27 home loss to Auburn.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU, and its two losses to Oklahoma and Florida were by three points each.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's road wins at Kentucky, LSU and Vanderbilt plus home routs of South Carolina and Texas A&M outweigh close losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 and added wins over Auburn, Kentucky, LSU, Texas A&M and Georgia Tech, with losses to Texas and South Carolina by a combined six points.
rationales.Ole Miss: Ole Miss beat Louisville, Missouri, Auburn and LSU, but the 7-42 home loss to Georgia and the 28-52 loss at Florida cap its case.
rationales.Oklahoma: Oklahoma beat Texas, Florida, Ole Miss and Texas A&M, though home losses to Kentucky and South Carolina and the Georgia rout are real drags.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss is 24-31 at Notre Dame, and it beat Wake Forest, Clemson, Duke, Pittsburgh and Florida State.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's lone loss is 24-28 at BYU, and it beat Miami, SMU, North Carolina, Wisconsin and Navy by comfortable margins.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 10-0 in FBS play with wins over BYU, Houston, Arizona, Cincinnati, Iowa State and TCU, though its schedule strength is modest.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win at Oregon and double-digit wins over Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois, Maryland and Michigan State, losing only 16-18 at Michigan.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana beat USC, Nebraska, Michigan, Northwestern and Minnesota, with its only losses to Ohio State by four and at Washington by three.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 in FBS play with wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State, Arizona State and Baylor, its lone loss 24-37 at Cincinnati.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina, and its only loss was a one-point home stumble to Auburn.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's only losses are a one-score home game to Georgia and at Tennessee, backed by road wins at LSU, Kentucky and Vanderbilt plus a 49-18 rout of South Carolina.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU, with its two losses both one-score games to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's only losses are one-score games to Texas and South Carolina, and it beat Alabama 26-10 and won at Auburn, Arkansas and Texas A&M.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with wins over BYU, Houston, Arizona, Iowa State and TCU, though its schedule lacks a marquee non-conference win.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with its only loss a one-score game at Notre Dame, plus wins over Clemson, Florida State and Wake Forest.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's lone loss is a one-score game at BYU, and it beat Miami head-to-head while dominating Wisconsin, SMU and Stanford.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a win over USC and close losses only to Ohio State and Washington, including a road win at Michigan.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win at Oregon and its only loss a two-point game at Michigan.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with its only loss to Miami, and it won at Louisville, SMU, NC State and Georgia Tech.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with its only loss at Cincinnati, and it beat Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Baylor.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a head-to-head win over Notre Dame and Arizona, with both losses on the road by one score.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia remains No. 1 after its 34-6 win over South Carolina, combining a 9-1 record, 23.9-point margin and victories over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri.
rationales.Utah: Utah's 40-39 road win over Arizona completes a 10-0 sweep with no losses, while its wins over BYU, Houston and Cincinnati give it the strongest unbeaten body of work.
rationales.Texas: Texas stays elite at 9-2 with a 15.1-point margin, and its wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU outweigh narrow losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 27-13 win over USC and earlier victory over Nebraska justify a top-five Big Ten placement, with an 8-2 record and 13.6-point margin.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State remains a top-five contender despite four losses, because wins over Iowa, Indiana, Illinois and Northwestern outweigh defeats to Oregon, USC, Texas and Nebraska.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's 41-28 win over Ohio State and 31-7 win over Michigan strengthen its case, while the 7-3 record and 21.3-point margin support a top-ten ranking.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record, 25.3-point margin and wins over Miami, Wisconsin, Stanford, Boston College and Navy make its lone loss to BYU manageable.
rationales.Miami: Miami's 9-1 record and 18.1-point margin are reinforced by wins over Clemson, Wake Forest, Stanford and Florida State, with only a narrow loss to Notre Dame.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's 10-1 record and 16.5-point margin, including wins over Oregon, Wisconsin, Maryland and Illinois, make it a deserving Big Ten top-ten team.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's wins over Alabama, Auburn, Kentucky, LSU and Texas A&M support an 8-2 case, though its loss to South Carolina prevents a higher finish.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 8-2 record and 16.9-point margin remain elite, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee and a weaker finish than the top teams prevent a top-ten spot.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech's 9-1 record, 13.3-point margin and wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Oregon State make it a strong résumé outside the top ten.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia remains No. 1 after beating Alabama, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina, with a 23.9-point FBS margin and six wins over fellow candidates.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 record, 13.6-point margin and wins over USC, Nebraska and Michigan justify a top-two place despite its narrow loss to Ohio State.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State has elite numbers and wins over Iowa and Indiana, but four losses, including Oregon and USC, keep it just behind Indiana.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa's eight wins, 12.3-point margin and road victory over Michigan support a top-five case, though the Ohio State loss and Minnesota loss prevent a higher spot.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's wins over Ohio State, USC and Michigan and 21.3 FPI make it a top-five contender despite narrow losses to UCLA and Illinois.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a 16.5-point margin, a road win over Oregon and convincing wins over Wisconsin, Illinois and Michigan State.
rationales.Texas: Texas has nine wins and quality victories over Ohio State, Tennessee, LSU and Ole Miss, with only Oklahoma and Florida causing losses.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's eight wins include Alabama, Auburn, LSU and Kentucky, giving it a stronger body of work than most teams below the top five.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 16.9-point margin and wins over Kentucky, South Carolina, LSU and Florida State offset losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with no losses, a 16.2-point margin and wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston and Cincinnati, making its No. 2 ranking difficult to sustain.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with an 18.1-point margin and wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Stanford and Florida State, with only Notre Dame defeating it.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a 25.3-point margin and wins over Miami, Wisconsin, Stanford and Boston College, but the BYU loss prevents a top-ten finish.

rationales.Utah: Utah stays unbeaten at 11-0 with a full Big 12 slate of quality wins (BYU, Arizona, Houston, TCU, Iowa State) and no losses, making the No. 1 case straightforward, though the one-point Arizona escape adds some uncertainty.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia's only blemish is a one-score home loss to Auburn, offset by road wins over Alabama, Ole Miss and South Carolina plus neutral-site Florida and home wins over Oklahoma and Missouri.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with its lone loss a competitive game at Notre Dame, and its wins over Clemson, Florida State, Duke and Pittsburgh anchor a strong ACC body of work.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a marquee win over Ohio State plus Tennessee, LSU and Ole Miss, and both losses (Oklahoma, Florida) came by a field goal, though the Florida home loss is a real blemish.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with the only loss a tight road game at BYU, and its home win over Miami plus a rout of SMU keep it firmly in the at-large conversation.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 9-2 with a strong SEC slate, but home loss to Georgia and a lopsided loss at Tennessee temper a resume that includes LSU, Texas A&M, South Carolina and Florida State wins.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with its only loss at Cincinnati, and wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Arizona State give it the Big 12's second-best profile behind Utah.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with the lone loss to Miami, and road wins over Louisville, SMU and Georgia Tech plus a 57-3 rout of Stanford make a compelling ACC case, though its schedule strength is the softest of the one-loss group.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with narrow losses to Ohio State and Washington, but the home win over USC and road win at Michigan keep it ahead of other two-loss Big Ten teams.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a signature home win over Alabama, and its losses to Texas and South Carolina were both by one score, though the South Carolina road loss stings.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a home win over Notre Dame and a win over Arizona, but the road loss to Utah and an upset loss at UCF leave it just outside the top ten.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 9-2 with wins over Michigan, Washington and Wisconsin, but a home loss to Ohio State and a one-score loss at Minnesota keep it at the back of the top 12.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia owns the best collection of direct wins among candidates, beating Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina, with only a one-score Auburn loss.
rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten and won every comparable Big 12 head-to-head, beating BYU, Houston and Arizona, so the perfect record and direct results carry the day.
rationales.Miami: Miami's lone loss came at Notre Dame, but its 33-20 win at Wake Forest and 41-13 rout at Clemson give it the strongest ACC direct evidence.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame beat Miami head-to-head 31-24 and its only loss is a four-point trip to BYU, so the direct win over Miami outweighs the comparable records.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss and Missouri directly, but the neutral loss to Oklahoma and home loss to Florida are real blemishes that keep it below the unbeatens.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 in FBS with direct wins over Houston and Arizona and a road rout of Oklahoma State, with only a Cincinnati loss marring the sheet.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame and Arizona head-to-head, but the road loss to Utah and the UCF defeat are why the Cougars sit behind the Utes despite quality wins.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 and beat Oregon 17-15 on the road, a direct result that outweighs the Ducks' stronger schedule; the only loss is an 18-16 trip to Michigan.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana beat USC 27-13 and lost only to Ohio State by four and Washington by three, so its direct win over the Trojans anchors this spot.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 and Kentucky 34-6 directly, but the home loss to Texas and road loss to South Carolina cap the Volunteers here.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's wins over Kentucky, South Carolina, LSU and Texas A&M are strong, but direct losses to Georgia and Tennessee keep the Tide behind both.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon beat Ohio State 41-28 on the road and USC 41-27 away, but the home loss to UCLA is a direct result that outweighs those wins.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia passes every visual test with an unblemished FBS conference slate punctuated by a decisive 34-6 road beatdown of South Carolina.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains undefeated at 11-0, displaying dominant complete-game control with a 38-17 road dismantling of TCU.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame looks like an absolute juggernaut on the field, shutting down SMU 24-3 while boasting a resume-topping win over Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami responded to their lone setback with explosive offensive execution and a steady multi-score profile across ACC competition.
rationales.Texas: Texas brings elite top-end athleticism, demonstrated by a commanding 45-3 blowout of Arkansas to reinforce their formidable profile.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama physically overwhelmed Chattanooga 47-0 and features one of the most imposing margins of victory against top-tier competition.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA slips after struggling to find offensive rhythm in an 18-16 road loss at Michigan, but their broader body of work remains stellar.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee showed suffocating defensive control in a convincing 27-13 home win over LSU to bolster their championship credentials.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech continues their dominant roll through Big 12 play, executing efficiently on both sides in a 20-10 victory over Baylor.
rationales.BYU: BYU proved their resilience yet again, holding off Kansas 31-29 on the road behind clutch fourth-quarter drives.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest operates with incredible offensive efficiency, running away with a 50-29 victory at Georgia Tech.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana suffered their first misstep in a tight 27-24 loss at Washington, though their physical style still demands immense respect.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's only loss came at home to Auburn and it closed with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida and Missouri by margins of 27 or more in most of them.
rationales.Miami: Miami beat Notre Dame 31-24 at home, Florida State 43-35 and Clemson 41-13, and its 10-1 record is paired with a 15-point win at Stanford.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's only loss is a 28-24 road defeat to BYU, and it won 41-13 over Wisconsin and 58-7 over Stanford in a dominant body of work.
rationales.Utah: Utah is undefeated, with a 28-20 home win over BYU and a 40-39 road survival at Arizona that shows it can win close games.
rationales.Texas: Texas holds a 24-23 home win over Ohio State and a 34-27 home win over Ole Miss, but its 2-point loss at home to Florida and its earlier loss to Oklahoma on a neutral field keep it below the top three.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama lost only at Tennessee and to Georgia by 3, but its 31-13 road win at LSU and 49-18 win over South Carolina are strong, and its 56-23 win at Mississippi State is a dominant road result.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State lost 23-24 at Texas and 28-41 at home to Oregon, but beat Iowa 31-14 on the road and USC 30-18 at home, which keeps it in the top group.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon lost at home to UCLA 15-17 and at Oklahoma State earlier, but it beat USC 41-27 and Ohio State 41-28 on the road, with a 34-27 home win over Boise State.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 19-15 road win at Ohio State and 27-13 home win over USC give it a useful quality profile, though its only other loss is a close one to Washington.
rationales.BYU: BYU's 28-24 home win over Notre Dame and 28-17 win over Arizona are strong, but its 20-28 road loss at Utah and 31-39 loss at UCF keep it below the elite teams.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's road win at Texas and 26-10 home win over Alabama are good, but its 6-34 road loss at Kentucky and 27-24 loss to South Carolina temper the case.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest won 57-3 at home over Stanford and 51-7 over Virginia, while its 33-20 home loss to Miami is its only defeat in a strong profile.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays atop the November 17 committee poll after beating South Carolina 34-6, with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, and Ole Miss and only a narrow Auburn loss.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains unbeaten at 10-0 against FBS teams, and its wins over BYU, Houston, and Arizona support the packet's No. 2 position despite a comparatively modest schedule proxy.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama holds third: its wins over LSU and Texas A&M and strong schedule offset losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame moves ahead of Miami on its 10-1 record and head-to-head win over the Hurricanes, reinforced by a 24-3 win over SMU.
rationales.Texas: Texas retains a top-five place with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, though losses to Oklahoma and Florida temper its case.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss is to Notre Dame, and its 9-1 FBS record plus wins over Clemson, Wake Forest, and Florida State keep it firmly in the field.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 FBS record includes road wins over Michigan and Nebraska and a win over USC, while its narrow home loss to Ohio State limits its ceiling.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon has a strong schedule and wins over Ohio State, USC, and Boise State, but its losses to UCLA, Illinois, and Oklahoma State keep it below the leading contenders.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's wins over Alabama, LSU, Kentucky, and Texas A&M outweigh its losses to Texas and South Carolina, though the latter is a damaging result.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 against FBS teams with wins over Arizona and Houston, but its road loss to Cincinnati and less imposing schedule hold it just outside the top eight.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's 10-1 record and road win over Oregon remain impressive, while a recent 18-16 loss at Michigan is the chief blemish.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest's 9-1 mark, dominant scoring margin, and road win at Louisville are strong, but its home loss to Miami and lighter schedule place it below the top tier.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays No. 1 after dismantling South Carolina 34-6, with a 10-1 resume headlined by wins over Alabama, Ole Miss, Missouri and Florida and the SEC's best scoring margin.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston, Iowa State and TCU, and the head-to-head edge over BYU keeps the Big 12's lone unbeaten at No. 2.
rationales.Texas: Texas moves up after routing Arkansas 45-3; wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, LSU, Ole Miss and Missouri outweigh one-score losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame beat SMU 24-3 to reach 10-1, and its home win over Miami plus a dominant body of work offsets the lone loss at BYU.
rationales.Miami: Miami handled Virginia Tech 28-20 to stay 10-1; the only loss is a close one at Notre Dame, with wins over Clemson, Florida State and Wake Forest.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 9-2 resume with wins over LSU, Florida State, Texas A&M and South Carolina holds at No. 6 despite losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest crushed Georgia Tech 50-29 to reach 10-1, with the lone loss to Miami and road wins over Louisville, SMU and NC State supporting a top-eight slot.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech beat Baylor 20-10 to finish 10-1, with only a loss at Cincinnati and wins over Arizona, Houston and Oklahoma State.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat LSU 27-13 to move to 9-2; the win over Alabama is strong, but losses to Texas and South Carolina keep it just outside the top eight.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's first loss, 16-18 at Michigan, drops it from No. 4, but a 10-1 resume with a win at Oregon and a top-tier scoring margin keeps it in the top 10.
rationales.BYU: BYU fell 29-31 at Kansas to slip to 9-2; wins over Notre Dame and Arizona remain strong, but the Utah and UCF losses are costly.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana lost 24-27 at Washington, its second one-score defeat alongside the Ohio State game, though the win over USC keeps it firmly in the field.

rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten at 10-0 against FBS teams and added a road win over Arizona, completing a 3-0 run against ranked Big 12 opponents.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia's 10-1 record includes wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, and Ole Miss, and its 34-6 win at South Carolina reinforces the strongest overall case.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with substantial wins over Clemson, Wake Forest, and Florida State; the road loss to Notre Dame is its only blemish.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 mark and 25.3 average FBS margin are backed by wins over Miami and SMU, though BYU remains a head-to-head loss.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1, has no one-score losses, and beat ranked Arizona and Houston, though its schedule case is less proven than the top four.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's wins over USC and Michigan and narrow road loss at Washington support 8-2, while Ohio State's head-to-head win over Indiana keeps this close; the modest brand preference breaks that close call for Indiana only because of its broader wins.
rationales.Texas: Texas has quality wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, but its two one-score losses include a head-to-head defeat by Oklahoma.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's 8-2 resume features a 26-10 win over Alabama and victories over LSU and Kentucky, offset by losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 9-1 with a 23.3 FBS average margin and a road win at Louisville, but its loss to Miami and comparatively modest schedule leave it below the top tier.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's wins over Ohio State and USC are excellent, but losses to UCLA, Illinois, and Oklahoma State keep it behind the unbeaten and stronger-record teams.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's wins over LSU, Texas A&M, and Florida State bolster its case, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee are significant, and Tennessee's direct win matters.
rationales.BYU: BYU's wins over Notre Dame and Arizona are strong, but the Utah loss and road defeat to UCF weigh on an otherwise 8-2 resume.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 9-1 against FBS teams, leads the packet’s SP+ (31.3) and FPI (28.675), and has beaten Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri; its only loss was a three-point home upset by Auburn.
rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten at 10-0 in FBS play, has the strongest listed schedule proxy among the unbeaten contenders, and owns wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston and Iowa State.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame’s 10-1 record, 25.6 SP+, 27.212 FPI, and wins over Miami, Wisconsin and SMU outweigh its four-point road loss to BYU.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with a 24.4 SP+ and 24.282 FPI, and its wins over Clemson, Wake Forest and Florida State support a high placement despite the road loss to Notre Dame.
rationales.Texas: Texas combines a 9-2 record and 0.5884 schedule proxy with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss and Missouri, though its narrow losses to Oklahoma and Florida prevent a higher slot.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon’s 0.6091 schedule proxy is the strongest listed, and wins over Ohio State, USC and Boise State support its standing despite losses to UCLA, Oklahoma State and Illinois.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana’s 8-2 record, 23.1 SP+ and 20.765 FPI are backed by wins over USC, Michigan and Nebraska; its close home loss to Ohio State is balanced by that resume.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 and has the head-to-head road win over Oregon, but its schedule proxy and ratings trail the teams above it, and it lost narrowly at Michigan.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama’s 22.9 SP+ and 24.21 FPI accompany wins over LSU, Texas A&M and Florida State, while losses to Georgia and Tennessee keep it behind teams with stronger records.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1, has a 19.4 SP+, and beat Houston, Arizona and Oklahoma State, but its schedule proxy is lower than those of several teams ranked ahead.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee’s 8-2 record and 21.5 SP+ are supported by wins over Alabama, LSU and Kentucky, although the home loss to Texas and road loss to South Carolina weigh on its case.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 9-1 with 22.6 SP+ and a 23.3 average FBS margin, but the home loss to Miami and weaker schedule proxy than the leading teams temper its ranking.

rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with a 21.7 SP+ and 19.4 FPI, the only unbeaten team, and its 40-39 road win at Arizona plus 28-20 home win over BYU give it the strongest measured body of work.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 at 24.4 SP+ and 24.3 FPI, with a road win over Notre Dame (31-24 vs. a 6-ranked opponent) and a road win at Clemson, making it the most efficient one-loss profile.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with 22.4 SP+ and 25.4 FPI, beating Ohio State, Florida, and Ole Miss, though its losses to Oklahoma and Florida keep it below the top tier.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with the highest SP+ (31.3) and FPI (28.7) in the packet, anchored by a neutral-site win over Florida and a 20-17 road win at Alabama; its lone loss at Auburn is its only blemish.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 at 25.6 SP+ and 27.2 FPI, with a strong 7-6 ranked-opponent record and wins over Miami and Michigan State, but its loss at BYU weighs on its resume.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 9-2 with 22.9 SP+ and 24.2 FPI, with strong wins at LSU and over Florida State, yet its losses to Georgia and Tennessee are both measurable resume blemishes.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State is 7-4 at 24.1 SP+ and 23.2 FPI, a strong efficiency profile whose losses to Texas, USC, and Oregon, plus a close 19-15 win over Indiana, cap its resume.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with 19.4 SP+ and 17.1 FPI, a one-loss profile built on wins over Arizona and Houston and a road win at Oklahoma State.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 at 23.1 SP+ and 20.8 FPI, with a narrow loss to Ohio State and wins over USC and Rutgers; its road losses are limited.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with 21.5 SP+ and 19.1 FPI, with a road win over Texas and a home win over Alabama offset by a loss at South Carolina.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 8-3 at 18.3 SP+ and 21.3 FPI, with road wins at USC and Ohio State but losses to Oklahoma State and Illinois keep its record weaker.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with 18.0 SP+ and 15.3 FPI, with a home win over Notre Dame and wins over Arizona and Arizona State, though losses to UCF and Utah trail peers.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays at number one with a sterling 10-1 record highlighted by head-to-head victories over Alabama and Oklahoma.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains undefeated at 11-0, backed by direct head-to-head wins over BYU and Houston.
rationales.Texas: Texas earns the third spot over other two-loss squads thanks to direct head-to-head wins over Tennessee and Ohio State.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame sits at number four on the strength of its 10-1 record and a 31-24 direct head-to-head win over Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami places fifth with a 10-1 ledger and a decisive 33-20 road head-to-head victory against Wake Forest.
rationales.BYU: BYU is sixth having beaten Notre Dame 28-24 head-to-head, though its loss to Utah keeps it behind the top tier.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech surges to seventh at 10-1 with solid Big 12 victories including a 28-26 head-to-head win over Houston.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama holds eighth, falling behind Texas due to Texas beating Tennessee, who defeated Alabama 26-10 head-to-head.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee takes ninth right behind Alabama, anchored by its direct 26-10 head-to-head victory over the Crimson Tide.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA drops to tenth following its defeat to Michigan, though it retains a direct 17-15 head-to-head win over Oregon.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is eleventh at 10-1, bolstered by a 30-27 direct road victory over ranked Louisville.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana rounds out the top twelve at 9-2, holding a crucial 27-13 head-to-head win over USC.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's lone loss is a 27-24 home stumble to Auburn, offset by road wins at Alabama, Ole Miss and South Carolina and a neutral win over Florida.
rationales.Texas: Texas owns a road win at Tennessee, a home win over Ole Miss and a road win at Missouri, with only narrow losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's two losses are to Georgia by three and at Tennessee, backed by road wins at Kentucky, LSU and Vanderbilt and a home win over Texas A&M.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 and handled Kentucky and Texas A&M on the road, with its only losses to Texas by three and at South Carolina.
rationales.Ole Miss: Ole Miss beat Louisville neutral, Missouri and LSU, but the head-to-head losses to Georgia, Oklahoma, Texas and Florida cap the case.
rationales.Oklahoma: Oklahoma's neutral win over Texas and home win over Ole Miss are strong, though home losses to Kentucky and South Carolina and a rout at Georgia weigh heavily.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 10-0 in FBS play with wins over BYU, Houston and Arizona, but the packet's schedule strength is thinner than the SEC contenders above.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss is at Notre Dame by seven, and road wins at Wake Forest, Clemson and Stanford plus a home win over Duke anchor a strong ACC case.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame beat Miami 31-24 and owns a 10-1 FBS mark, but the road loss at BYU and a softer schedule keep it behind the SEC and Miami.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 in FBS with wins over Houston and Arizona, but the lone loss at Cincinnati and a modest schedule strength temper the resume.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana beat USC and Michigan on the road and Nebraska away, but the home loss to Ohio State and the road loss at Washington limit the top-line case.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame and Arizona and won at TCU and Kansas, but the road losses to Utah and UCF keep it below the one-loss contenders.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with the packet's best win list, including Alabama at home, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri, and its only loss is a one-score home upset by Auburn.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with no losses, quality wins over BYU, Houston, Arizona, Iowa State and TCU, and five road-or-neutral wins.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 9-2 resume includes road wins at Kentucky, LSU and Vanderbilt plus a 49-18 handling of South Carolina, with only one-score losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a win over Ohio State, road wins at Tennessee, LSU and Missouri, and only one-score losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a marquee win over Miami and dominant victories over Wisconsin, SMU and Stanford, losing only a one-score game at BYU.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Duke and Florida State, and its lone loss is a one-score game at Notre Dame.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a home win over Alabama plus Auburn, LSU and Texas A&M, with narrow losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with no one-score losses, wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Arizona State, and its only loss came at Cincinnati.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a head-to-head win over Notre Dame plus Arizona, Arizona State, TCU and Iowa State, losing only to Utah and UCF.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a win over USC and road wins at Nebraska and Michigan, with one-score losses only to Ohio State and Washington.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road-or-neutral wins, including Louisville, SMU and Virginia, and its only loss is to Miami.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 8-3 but its three losses are all one-score games, and it owns road wins over Ohio State, USC and Michigan State.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia remains No. 1 with a 23.9-point FBS margin, a 9-1 record, and wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri, and South Carolina since the November 17 poll.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State has the strongest Big Ten case at 7-4, a 14.7-point margin, and quality wins over Iowa and Indiana, despite losses to Oregon, USC, Texas, and Nebraska.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 record, 13.6-point margin, and wins over Nebraska, Michigan, Northwestern, and USC support a top-five ranking despite its close loss to Ohio State.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 7-3 with a 21.3-point margin and wins over Ohio State, USC, Michigan, and Michigan State, though its upset losses to UCLA and Oklahoma State temper the case.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a 16.5-point margin, a road win over Oregon, and wins over Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, and Maryland, with only a narrow loss to Michigan.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 8-2 with a 12.3-point margin and quality wins over Michigan, Wisconsin, Northwestern, Illinois, and Purdue, earning the benefit of the doubt after its loss to Ohio State.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a 15.1-point margin and wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU, although its Oklahoma loss and Florida loss prevent a higher placement.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a 25.3-point margin and a win over Miami, but a loss to BYU and a late loss to Boston College keep it just outside the top eight.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with an 18.1-point margin and wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Florida State, and Pittsburgh, with its only loss coming against Notre Dame.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with a 16.2-point margin and wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston, and Cincinnati, making it the packet's only undefeated candidate and a strong top-ten case.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 8-2 with a 13.8-point margin and wins over Alabama, Auburn, Kentucky, LSU, and Texas A&M, though its loss to South Carolina and narrow loss to Texas count against it.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 8-2 with a 16.9-point margin and quality wins over Kentucky, South Carolina, LSU, and Florida State, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee keep it outside the playoff top 10.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 9-1 with a 23.9-point FBS margin, and its post-poll wins over Ole Miss, Missouri, and South Carolina reinforce an elite case despite the Auburn loss.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State moves up because its 41-28 win at Oregon and 31-14 win at Iowa provide major quality evidence that the November 17 poll did not fully reflect.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 27-13 defeat of USC and 20-17 road win over Nebraska strengthen its Big Ten case, while the loss to Ohio State keeps it below the top two.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's wins over USC and Ohio State and 41-28 victory at Illinois showcase a strong Big Ten body of work, though the UCLA loss prevents a top-five finish.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA remains 10-1 with a 16.5-point margin, and its road win over Oregon plus wins over Illinois and Michigan State outweigh the narrow Michigan loss.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 10-0 with no losses, four road or neutral wins, and a 16.2-point margin, making its unbeaten record the strongest counterargument to Georgia's higher standing.
rationales.Texas: Texas pairs a 9-2 record with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU, although the Oklahoma loss prevents a top-five placement.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record, 25.3-point margin, and 31-24 win over Miami outweigh the narrow loss to BYU and justify a top-eight case.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with a 18.1-point margin, six road or neutral wins, and a head-to-head win over Wake Forest, though the Notre Dame loss prevents a higher spot.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech has won nine of ten, produced a 13.3-point margin, and beaten Houston, Arizona, and Oklahoma State without a one-score loss.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's wins over Alabama, Auburn, Kentucky, LSU, and Texas A&M support a top-12 case, but the South Carolina loss and narrow Texas defeat temper it.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa's 8-2 record, 12.3-point margin, and road wins over Michigan, Washington, Northwestern, and Illinois earn Big Ten benefit of the doubt after its November 17 No. 15 ranking.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with the nation's best scoring margin and wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri and Florida, with the lone blemish a one-score home loss to Auburn.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with zero one-score losses and quality wins over BYU, Arizona, Iowa State, TCU and Houston, though its schedule strength is modest and we note some uncertainty about depth of opposition.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with the only loss a four-point road defeat at BYU, plus wins over Miami, Wisconsin, SMU and a decisive Navy neutral-site result.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with a dominant profile (24.4 SP+) and wins over Clemson, Florida State and Wake Forest, its only loss a seven-point road game at Notre Dame — the head-to-head favors the Irish.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with elite wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, LSU, Ole Miss and Missouri, though its two losses (Oklahoma, Florida) are to teams with losing SEC records.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 9-2 with a strong SEC body of work (LSU, Texas A&M, South Carolina, Florida State), but the 26-10 loss at Tennessee and the close Georgia defeat temper its case.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with no one-score losses and wins over Arizona, Houston, Oklahoma State and Arizona State; its lone loss came at unranked Cincinnati.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with wins over USC, Michigan and Nebraska, its two losses a four-point home game against Ohio State and a three-point road loss at Washington.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a signature home win over Notre Dame and a win over Arizona, but the road loss to unranked UCF is a notable blemish alongside the Utah defeat.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win at Oregon and wins over Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota; its lone loss is a two-point road defeat at Michigan, though its schedule is the softest among one-loss teams.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road/neutral wins including Louisville, SMU and Georgia Tech, its only loss a 13-point home game against Miami.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a head-to-head win over Alabama plus Auburn, LSU and Kentucky wins, offset by narrow losses to Texas and South Carolina.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia owns the strongest direct resume: wins at Alabama, at Ole Miss, over Oklahoma, and at South Carolina, with the lone loss to Auburn; the head-to-head edge over Alabama and Tennessee settles the top.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 and swept its direct tests over BYU, Houston, and Arizona, so the unbeaten record plus head-to-head wins outweigh Georgia's deeper schedule.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss came at Notre Dame, but the Hurricanes beat Wake Forest 33-20 head-to-head; with comparable records and schedule strength, the direct win over a fellow contender drives this placement.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame beat Miami 31-24 head-to-head and holds ten FBS wins, but the road loss at BYU is the counterweight; the Miami win edges the Irish ahead of Texas on comparable resumes.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri directly, but the neutral loss to Oklahoma and home loss to Florida break the resume; the quality wins still keep the Longhorns ahead of Texas Tech.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with direct wins over Houston and Arizona and a road win at Oklahoma State, so its head-to-head edges over those Big 12 contenders outweigh the one loss at Cincinnati.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest beat Louisville 30-27 head-to-head and owns a 9-1 FBS mark, but the home loss to Miami is the tiebreaker that keeps the Demon Deacons behind the Hurricanes.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame 28-24 and Arizona 28-17 head-to-head, but the road losses to Utah and UCF and a thin margin profile keep the Cougars below the one-loss contenders.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 and beat Oregon 17-15 on the road, so the direct win over a ranked Oregon team outweighs the one-point loss at Michigan and lifts the Bruins above the Ducks.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana beat USC 27-13 head-to-head and holds eight FBS wins, but the home loss to Ohio State and road loss at Washington keep the Hoosiers behind UCLA's stronger record.
rationales.Ole Miss: Ole Miss beat Louisville and Missouri directly, but losses to Georgia, Texas, Oklahoma, and Florida are too many; the head-to-head wins over Louisville and Missouri place the Rebels ahead of both.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 head-to-head and has eight FBS wins, but the home loss to Texas and road loss at South Carolina are direct results that keep the Volunteers behind Texas.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia passes every physical eye test with dominant margins against top opponents and a decisive 34-6 road rout at South Carolina.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains flawless on the field, repeatedly displaying late-game poise and controlling the line of scrimmage against quality Big 12 opposition.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame looks like a complete powerhouse, stacking suffocating blowouts alongside signature top-ten victories over Miami and Wisconsin.
rationales.Miami: Miami controls opponents with an overwhelming offense, owning convincing double-digit victories over Clemson and Wake Forest.
rationales.Texas: Texas showcases elite playmakers and strong road mettle, punctuated by an emphatic 45-3 blowout over Arkansas.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama flashes devastating speed and a monstrous scoring margin, though occasional defensive lulls leave them just behind the top tier.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA has displayed great defensive identity and efficiency away from home, highlighted by winning at Oregon.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee possesses an explosive offense and brutal line play, evidenced by physically punishing Alabama and Kentucky.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech passes the visual test convincingly, overwhelming opponents with high-flying scoring and a 9-1 FBS mark.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest operates with crisp execution, repeatedly dismantling conference opponents by massive blowout margins.
rationales.BYU: BYU shows tremendous grit and tough physical football, backed up by a marquee home victory over Notre Dame.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana executes at a high level defensively despite falling in a tight battle against Washington.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's 9-1 FBS mark includes a 20-17 road win at Alabama and a 42-7 rout at Ole Miss, with margins dominating nearly every game.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with a 24-31 loss at Notre Dame as its only setback, and its wins over Clemson 41-13 and Florida State 43-35 show a team that wins big on the road.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record includes a 41-7 win over Boston College and a 31-24 road win at Miami, though its season-opening 28-24 win over BYU came at home.
rationales.Texas: Texas has beaten Ohio State 24-23 and Oklahoma's 27-24 win is a neutral-site result, but close losses to Florida 24-27 keep its margin profile thinner than the top three.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State's 28-41 home loss to Oregon and 15-19 loss to Indiana are unfavorable, yet its wins over Iowa 31-14 and USC 30-18 at home are real signals.
