rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a top-tier SEC resume: wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, LSU, Ole Miss and Missouri, with both losses (Oklahoma, Florida) by a field goal; the Ohio State win travels better than any Miami or Notre Dame non-conference result.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's two losses are to Georgia by three and at Tennessee, but the Tide own LSU, Texas A&M, South Carolina, Florida State and Kentucky; the 49-18 South Carolina win and 31-13 LSU road win keep them ahead of one-loss ACC and Big 12 teams with softer slates.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a home win over Alabama and road wins at Arkansas and Texas A&M; the losses (Texas by three, South Carolina by three) are both one-score, and the 34-6 Kentucky win since the last poll reinforces the profile.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with its only loss at Cincinnati, and the Red Raiders' wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State, Arizona State and Colorado give them the Big 12's deepest win list behind Utah.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road wins and a 23.3 average margin, but the lone loss came at home to Miami and the schedule (SMU, Louisville, Stanford, Virginia) trails the SEC and Big Ten contenders; the 50-29 Georgia Tech win caps a strong stretch.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with the only loss a two-point game at Michigan, plus a road win at Oregon and wins over Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota; the resume supports a move up from the AP's No. 10 given the record and road-heavy profile.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a head-to-head win over Notre Dame and wins over Arizona, Arizona State, TCU and Iowa State; the losses to Utah and UCF are both on the road, keeping the Cougars just ahead of the Big Ten two-loss trio.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a win over USC and narrow losses to Ohio State and Washington; the late road loss at Washington is the reason the Hoosiers sit behind BYU despite matching records.

rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten at 10-0 against FBS opponents, with wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston and Iowa State, and no losses to offset its strong body of work.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia's 9-1 FBS record includes road wins over Alabama and Ole Miss and decisive victories over Oklahoma, Florida and Missouri; its only loss is a one-score defeat to Auburn.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame pairs a 10-1 record and dominant scoring margin with wins over Miami and SMU, while its lone loss to BYU is a close road result.
rationales.Miami: Miami's 9-1 record features wins over Clemson, Wake Forest and Florida State, and its road loss to Notre Dame is counterbalanced by a strong schedule and consistent margins.
rationales.Texas: Texas has an excellent 9-2 record and wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss and Missouri, though narrow defeats to Oklahoma and Florida temper the case; its packet evidence edges comparable contenders.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's wins over Ohio State, USC and Boise State and its solid overall profile outweigh losses to UCLA, Illinois and Oklahoma State; the Texas preference is not enough to overcome its stronger case here.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win over Oregon and multiple convincing victories, with only a narrow loss at Michigan, making its resume stronger than the prior poll suggested.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 FBS record includes wins over USC, Michigan and Nebraska, while its close loss to Ohio State and road defeat at Washington keep it just below the top tier.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's wins over LSU, Florida State and Texas A&M stand out, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee leave it behind the teams with fewer setbacks; its brand tips a close comparison over Tennessee.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's wins over Alabama, LSU and Kentucky are substantial, but the South Carolina loss and close defeat to Texas place it narrowly behind Alabama in a comparable resume evaluation.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with a clean record against ranked Arizona and Houston and several convincing wins, but its schedule and overall case fall just short of the leading one-loss teams.
rationales.BYU: BYU's wins over Notre Dame, Arizona and Iowa State are impressive, but the road loss to Utah and setback at UCF leave it behind teams with stronger overall records.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia pairs a 9-1 FBS record and 23.9 average margin with the packet’s top SP+ (31.3) and FPI (28.675), plus wins over Alabama and five other ranked-reference opponents; the Auburn loss is outweighed by the full body of work.
rationales.Utah: Utah is unbeaten against FBS teams, has a 16.2 average margin, and combines top-tier SP+ and FPI with head-to-head wins over BYU, Houston, and Arizona, although the Utah case has less SOS support than Georgia’s.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame’s 10-1 mark, 25.3 margin, and elite ratings (SP+ 25.6; FPI 27.212) are reinforced by the Miami win and a decisive SMU victory, while its only loss was a four-point road defeat at BYU.
rationales.Texas: Texas brings a 9-2 record, strong 0.5884 SOS proxy and high SP+/FPI, plus wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU; its losses to Oklahoma and Florida keep it below the leading undefeated teams.
rationales.Miami: Miami’s 9-1 record, 18.1 margin, and strong ratings sit alongside wins over Wake Forest and Clemson; the Notre Dame loss is tempered by Miami’s road win at Wake and head-to-head victory over Florida State.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana’s 8-2 FBS record and 13.6 margin are supported by the second-best SP+ among candidates (23.1), high FPI, and wins over USC, Michigan, and Nebraska; the close Ohio State loss and Washington defeat limit its placement.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama’s 8-2 record and 0.53 SOS proxy include a road win over LSU and decisive wins over Kentucky and South Carolina, but its losses to Georgia and Tennessee leave it behind teams with better overall records and/or stronger efficiency measures.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon’s 7-3 mark has a high 0.6091 SOS proxy and wins over Ohio State, USC, and Boise State; losses to UCLA, Illinois, and Oklahoma State, plus a 21.349 FPI, hold it below the top six.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA’s 10-1 record and 16.5 margin include a road head-to-head win over Oregon and an SP+ of 21.1, but its 0.438 SOS proxy and modest FPI make the résumé less robust than the teams above it.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with no one-score losses, a 13.3 scoring margin, and wins over Arizona and Houston; its 19.4 SP+ helps offset a lower 0.47 SOS proxy and the loss at Cincinnati.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee’s 8-2 record includes a 26-10 win over Alabama and wins over LSU and Kentucky, but the losses to Texas and South Carolina and a lower FPI than nearby contenders reduce its standing.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest has a 9-1 record, 23.3 margin, and strong SP+ of 22.6, with a road win over Louisville; its 0.43 SOS proxy and head-to-head loss to Miami weigh against a higher slot.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia leads on SP+ (31.3) and FPI (28.7) with a 23.9 mean FBS margin, and its 20-17 win at Alabama and 27-8 neutral win over Florida anchor a strong resume despite the Auburn loss.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 10-0 in FBS games with a 16.2 mean margin and a 40-39 road win at Arizona, but its SP+ (21.7) and FPI (19.4) sit well below the top tier, so it ranks second on resume rather than efficiency.
rationales.Texas: Texas owns the nation's best-rated FPI tier among non-Georgia teams (25.4) and wins over Ohio State and Ole Miss, offset by losses to Oklahoma and Florida by three points each.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame has the highest scoring margin among the top group (25.3 mean), with a 31-24 win over Miami and 10-1 FBS record, though its loss at BYU keeps it below the top three.
rationales.Miami: Miami posts SP+ 24.4 and FPI 24.3 with an 18.1 mean margin and a 9-1 FBS record, but its best win list lacks a top-10 opponent beyond Notre Dame, where it lost.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State's 7-4 record carries four losses, yet SP+ (24.1) and FPI (23.2) are strong and its ranked-opponent wins include USC and Iowa.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama has a 9-2 record and SP+ of 22.9, with a 56-23 road win over Mississippi State, but two losses to ranked SEC teams cap its rank.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a 13.8 mean margin, a win over Alabama, and SP+ of 21.5, but its losses to Texas and South Carolina weigh it down.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with SP+ 23.1 and FPI 20.8, and beat ranked USC and Ohio State, though its FBS strength of schedule proxy is middling.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with SP+ 19.4, its best win over Arizona and a 52-27 road win at Oklahoma State, with only the Cincinnati loss on the ledger.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with SP+ 18.0 and FPI 15.3, and holds road-or-neutral wins over Kansas and Colorado State, but lost to Utah and UCF.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with an FBS record of 9-1 and a 23.3 mean margin, but its SP+ (22.6) and only win over a ranked opponent (Louisville) lag behind the top tier.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia holds the nation's premier resume at 10-1 with a direct 20-17 victory over Alabama.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains undefeated at 11-0 with definitive head-to-head wins over ranked BYU and Arizona.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 highlighted by their crucial 31-24 head-to-head victory over Miami.
rationales.Miami: Miami boasts a stellar 10-1 record with their top-tier win coming directly against Wake Forest, 33-20.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest stands at 10-1 with a signature 30-27 road win over Louisville, falling only to Miami.
rationales.BYU: BYU owns an elite 28-24 head-to-head triumph over Notre Dame to anchor their 9-2 resume.
rationales.Texas: Texas has high-profile victories including a 20-17 direct win at Tennessee and beating Ohio State.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee sits at 9-2 backed by an impressive 26-10 head-to-head win over Alabama.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama features a dominant 45-17 road win at Kentucky, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee cap their ceiling.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA carries a 10-1 record featuring a key 17-15 head-to-head road win over Oregon.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana holds a strong 9-2 record with a decisive 27-13 head-to-head victory against USC.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 overall and defeated conference rival Houston head-to-head, 28-26.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia owns the best win set in the packet, beating Alabama on the road plus Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina, with only a one-score home loss to Auburn.
rationales.Texas: Texas has the strongest cross-conference road win at Ohio State plus wins at Tennessee and LSU and over Ole Miss and Missouri, with its two losses coming by three points each.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's road wins at Kentucky, LSU, Mississippi State and Vanderbilt and a home rout of South Carolina outweigh narrow losses to Georgia and at Tennessee.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10, added wins over LSU, Auburn and Kentucky and won at Texas A&M and Georgia Tech, with losses by three points to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Utah: Utah is the only unbeaten resume, sweeping BYU, Houston, Arizona, Cincinnati, Iowa State and TCU, though the schedule strength proxy is modest relative to the SEC contenders.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 mark with a win over Miami and a blowout of Wisconsin is strong, but the head-to-head loss at BYU keeps the Irish below the one-loss SEC and Big 12 leaders.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 against FBS with road wins at Wake Forest, Clemson and Stanford, but the head-to-head loss at Notre Dame is the decisive separator.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's 10-1 record and road win at Oregon are excellent, yet the schedule proxy is low and the only loss came at Michigan by two points.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's wins at Michigan and Nebraska plus a home rout of USC are strong, but the home loss to Ohio State and road loss at Washington cap the case.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame head-to-head and swept Arizona, Arizona State, TCU, Iowa State and Kansas, but the loss at Utah and a road loss at UCF hold the Cougars back.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 against FBS with wins over Houston and Arizona and a road rout of Oklahoma State, with only a road loss at Cincinnati.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest's 10-1 mark includes a road win at Louisville and a rout of SMU, but the home loss to Miami is the head-to-head anchor.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with the best scoring margin in the packet, a road win at Alabama, and dominant wins over Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri, and South Carolina.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's 9-2 resume includes wins over LSU, Texas A&M, Florida State, South Carolina, and Vanderbilt, with only narrow losses to Georgia and Tennessee.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a win over Ohio State, road wins at Tennessee and LSU, and only two one-score losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a statement home win over Alabama plus wins at Georgia Tech and Texas A&M, its losses both one-score games.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with wins over BYU, Houston, Iowa State, and a one-point road win at Arizona, the only unbeaten FBS resume in the packet.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a win over Miami and blowouts of Wisconsin, SMU, and Stanford, its lone loss a four-point game at BYU.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with road wins at Wake Forest and Clemson and a win over Florida State, losing only by a touchdown at Notre Dame.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road or neutral wins including Louisville and SMU, its only loss a home game against Miami.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State, and Arizona State, its only loss at Cincinnati.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with wins over Notre Dame and Arizona plus a road win at Kansas, with losses to Utah and UCF.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a win over USC and road wins at Nebraska and Michigan, its losses to Ohio State and Washington both one-score games.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 9-2 with road wins at Michigan, Washington, and Illinois plus a win over Iowa State, losing only to Ohio State and Minnesota.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia pairs a 9-1 FBS record and 23.9-point margin with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri, plus a 34-6 finale over South Carolina.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a 25.3-point margin, a 41-13 neutral-site win over Wisconsin and a 31-24 home win over Miami, with only a road loss to BYU.
rationales.Utah: Utah is undefeated at 11-0, has no losses, and closes with wins over BYU and Arizona while also beating Houston, Cincinnati and TCU.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with a 15.1-point margin and strong road wins over Tennessee, Missouri and LSU, offset by losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State earns a Big Ten benefit of the doubt on a 7-4 record, 14.7-point margin, wins over Iowa and Indiana, and a challenging schedule featuring Oregon, USC, Texas and Nebraska.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 8-2 with a 13.6-point margin, road wins over Nebraska and Michigan, a home win over USC and a close loss to Ohio State.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 7-3 with an 8.6-point margin and quality wins over Ohio State, USC and Michigan, though its losses to UCLA, Oklahoma State and Illinois prevent a higher placement.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with an 18.1-point margin, a 52-23 win over Pittsburgh and a 43-35 win over Florida State, with its only loss to Notre Dame.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 9-1 with a 23.3-point margin and six road or neutral wins, including a 49-7 victory over SMU and a 50-29 win over Georgia Tech.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 8-2 with a 13.8-point margin and wins over Alabama, Auburn, Kentucky and LSU, despite narrow losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a 16.5-point margin, a 17-15 road win over Oregon and convincing wins over Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois and Maryland.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 8-2 with a 16.9-point margin and quality wins over Kentucky, South Carolina, LSU, Florida State and Texas A&M, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee keep it below the top ten.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia pairs a 9-1 FBS record with a 23.9-point margin, the packet's best rating profile, and wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, Missouri, and South Carolina.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a 25.3-point margin and wins over Miami, Stanford, Wisconsin, and Boston College, with only a BYU loss preventing perfection.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0, has no losses, and owns wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston, and Arkansas that sharpen its case beyond the AP's second-place ranking.
rationales.Texas: Texas sits 9-2 with quality wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU, offset by narrow losses to Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 9-1 with an 18.1-point margin and wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Duke, and Stanford, though its loss to Notre Dame prevents a clean case for the top five.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with no one-score losses, a 13.3-point margin, and wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State, and Oregon State.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 record and 13.6-point margin are reinforced by wins over USC, Nebraska, Michigan, and Northwestern, meriting a Big Ten benefit of the doubt.
rationales.Ohio State: Ohio State has a 23.2 FPI and strong wins over Iowa, Indiana, Illinois, and Northwestern, but losses to Oregon, USC, Nebraska, and Texas limit the case.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon is 7-3 with wins over Ohio State, USC, Michigan, and Nebraska, though its narrow UCLA loss and Illinois defeat keep it below the top eight.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 8-2 with a 12.3-point margin and wins over Michigan, Washington, Wisconsin, Northwestern, and Illinois, giving the Big Ten a credible No. 10 case.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 8-2 with a 16.9-point margin and wins over Kentucky, South Carolina, LSU, and Florida State, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee prevent a top-10 placement.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 8-2 with wins over Alabama, Auburn, Kentucky, and LSU, although close losses to Texas and South Carolina expose some vulnerability.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia is 10-1 with road wins over Alabama, Ole Miss and South Carolina and the SEC's best scoring margin; the lone Auburn loss is the only blemish on an otherwise complete resume.
rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 with wins over BYU, Houston, Iowa State, TCU and a one-point road win at Arizona, though several victories were narrow and the schedule lacks a top-tier nonconference win.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with its only loss at Notre Dame, which it can offset with the head-to-head tiebreaker plus road wins at Clemson, Wake Forest and Stanford and a strong ACC finish.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a home win over Miami and dominant wins over Wisconsin, USC-adjacent competition and SMU; the one-score loss at BYU keeps it just behind the Hurricanes.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with its only loss to Miami and impressive road wins over Louisville, SMU and Georgia Tech, though the ACC slate lacks other elite wins.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with its only loss at Cincinnati, holding wins over Houston, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Arizona State in a solid Big 12 run.
rationales.Texas: Texas is 9-2 with wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU; the Oklahoma and Florida losses are both one-score games.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama is 9-2 with road wins at Kentucky, LSU and Vanderbilt and a home win over Texas A&M, but home losses to Georgia and at Tennessee cost it seeding position.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee is 9-2 with a home win over Alabama and a win over Texas A&M, offset by a home loss to Texas and a road loss at South Carolina.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a signature home win over Notre Dame and a win over Arizona, but losses to Utah and UCF leave it behind the other one-loss and two-loss contenders.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a home win over USC and road wins at Nebraska and Michigan, with both losses (Ohio State, Washington) by a combined seven points.
rationales.Iowa: Iowa is 9-2 with a road win at Michigan and a win over Washington, and its only losses are to Ohio State and a one-point road loss at Minnesota.

rationales.Utah: Utah is 11-0 and owns direct wins over BYU, Houston, and Arizona, so its unbeaten record and head-to-head edge anchor the top spot.
rationales.Georgia: Georgia's only loss is to Auburn, and its road win at Alabama plus dominant wins over Oklahoma, Ole Miss, and Missouri make it the strongest one-loss SEC case.
rationales.Texas: Texas beat Ohio State, Tennessee, and Ole Miss head-to-head; the Oklahoma and Florida losses are offset by that quality-win stack and strong schedule.
rationales.Miami: Miami is 10-1 with a road win at Wake Forest and a blowout of Clemson; its lone loss at Notre Dame is the résumé's main blemish.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame beat Miami head-to-head and owns a 10-1 record, but the road loss at BYU keeps it behind the Hurricanes' overall body.
rationales.BYU: BYU beat Notre Dame and Arizona directly, but the head-to-head loss at Utah and the UCF loss cap its ceiling.
rationales.Ole Miss: Ole Miss beat Louisville and Missouri, but losses to Georgia, Texas, Oklahoma, and Florida make the head-to-head wins insufficient for a higher slot.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a direct road win at Oregon; the narrow Michigan loss is the only defeat and the Oregon result drives this placement.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon beat Ohio State and USC head-to-head, but the home loss to UCLA and the Illinois loss keep the Ducks behind the Bruins.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with direct wins over Houston and Arizona; the Cincinnati loss is the lone blemish and the head-to-head edges carry it.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest beat Louisville head-to-head and is 10-1, but the direct loss to Miami keeps the Demon Deacons below the Hurricanes.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama beat Kentucky and South Carolina but lost to Georgia and Tennessee head-to-head, so those direct results hold it below the SEC leaders.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia holds the nation's premier resume, dominant underlying metrics, and elite victories over Alabama and Ole Miss by large margins.
rationales.Utah: Utah is a perfect 11-0 with a stellar +16.2 scoring margin and head-to-head triumphs against BYU and Houston.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's dominant +25.3 average scoring margin and head-to-head win over Miami give them immense visual and physical appeal.
rationales.Miami: Miami boasts a sparkling +18.1 margin and high-end road victories over Wake Forest and Clemson.
rationales.Texas: Texas possesses exceptional top-end wins over Tennessee and Ohio State while scoring decisively on opponents all season.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama features an imposing +16.9 average scoring margin and blowout victories over Kentucky, South Carolina, and LSU.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA sits at 10-1 with an impressive road victory at Oregon and a stout defense driving a +16.5 point differential.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee dominates opponents at the line of scrimmage, highlighted by double-digit wins over Alabama and LSU.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech passes the eye test with a 10-1 record, a +13.3 margin, and high-scoring wins over Houston and Arizona.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest lights up the scoreboard with an explosive offense, compiling a +23.3 average margin and a road victory at Louisville.
rationales.BYU: BYU owns marquee wins over Notre Dame and Arizona with a physical style of play and an 8-2 FBS mark.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana controls games through a physical defense and a +13.6 margin, backed by a convincing double-digit win against USC.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's closing 48-21 and 42-7 wins over Missouri and Ole Miss, plus a 20-17 road win at Alabama, are the most dominant closing margins in the packet.
rationales.Utah: Utah is undefeated at 11-0 with a 40-39 road win at Arizona and a 28-20 home win over BYU, though no win in the packet exceeds 10 points of margin against a ranked opponent.
rationales.Texas: Texas owns a 34-27 win over Ole Miss and a 34-20 road win at Missouri, but its 24-27 home loss to Florida and 24-27 neutral loss to Oklahoma show close games.
rationales.Miami: Miami's 10-1 record includes a 31-24 home loss to Notre Dame and wins of 52-23 over Pittsburgh and 43-35 over Florida State, with a dominant 52-3 over Central Michigan.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame is 10-1 with a 31-24 home win over Miami and a 41-13 neutral win over Wisconsin, but its only loss is a 24-28 road defeat at BYU.

rationales.Oregon: Oregon's 41-28 road win at Ohio State and 41-27 home win over USC are strong, offset by a 10-21 loss at Illinois and a 31-39 loss at Oklahoma State.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee won 26-10 at home over Alabama and 34-6 over Kentucky, but its 17-20 home loss to Texas and 24-27 road loss at South Carolina leave it a notch behind.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech beat Houston 28-26 and Arizona 34-26 at home, and its 53-25 win over Arizona State and 52-27 road win at Oklahoma State show its offense can run away from opponents.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest won 57-3 over Stanford and 49-7 at SMU but lost 20-33 at home to Miami, and its best road win is 30-27 at Louisville.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 27-13 home win over USC and 15-19 home loss to Ohio State are both one-score results, but it has been dominant in its wins over Rutgers and Western Kentucky.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA beat Oregon 17-15 on the road and Wisconsin 17-7 at home, but its 16-18 road loss at Michigan and tight wins limit its margin profile.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia stays atop the AP anchor after beating South Carolina 34-6, with wins over Alabama, Oklahoma, Florida, Ole Miss, and Missouri and its only loss to Auburn.
rationales.Utah: Utah remains unbeaten at 11-0 after beating TCU 38-17, and its wins over BYU, Arizona, Houston, and Iowa State strengthen a clean résumé.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record and wins over Miami, Wisconsin, and SMU offset the BYU loss; its 31-24 head-to-head win over Miami is decisive here.
rationales.Miami: Miami's only loss is to Notre Dame, while wins over Wake Forest, Clemson, Florida State, and Duke support its top-four position despite the head-to-head setback.
rationales.Texas: Texas rebounded from its close losses to Oklahoma and Florida with wins over Missouri, LSU, and Arkansas, and has a high-value victory over Ohio State.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's losses to Georgia and Tennessee are counterbalanced by wins over LSU, Texas A&M, Florida State, and Mississippi State, though its 17-20 loss to Georgia keeps it below Texas.

rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win over Oregon and a strong scoring résumé; its only defeat was a narrow road loss to Michigan.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest's 9-1 record features a road win over Louisville and blowout wins over SMU and Virginia, but its loss to Miami and lighter schedule keep it outside the byes.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana has useful wins over USC, Michigan, and Nebraska, but its Ohio State loss and late 24-27 defeat at Washington temper the AP position.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with wins over Arizona, Houston, and Oklahoma State, but its loss to Cincinnati and relatively modest schedule profile limit its ceiling.

rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's 9-2 resume includes wins over Alabama, Auburn, LSU and Texas A&M, with narrow losses to Texas and South Carolina.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 10-1 with the only loss a road upset at Cincinnati, backed by wins over Houston, Arizona, Arizona State and Oklahoma State.
rationales.Wake Forest: Wake Forest is 10-1 with six road/neutral wins and a 49-7 rout of SMU; the home loss to Miami is its lone blemish.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA is 10-1 with a road win at Oregon and wins over Wisconsin, Illinois and Minnesota, though its schedule ranks softer than peers ahead.
rationales.BYU: BYU is 9-2 with a signature win over Notre Dame and a sweep of Arizona, Arizona State and Baylor; losses to Utah and UCF cap it.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana is 9-2 with a win over USC, but the week-12 road loss at Washington and the one-score Ohio State defeat keep it at the bottom of the bye line.

rationales.Georgia: Georgia's only loss was a one-point home defeat to Auburn, while wins over Alabama, Tennessee, and Ole Miss anchor an otherwise dominant resume.
rationales.Notre Dame: Notre Dame's 10-1 record includes a win over Miami and a neutral-site win over Wisconsin, with its only defeat a narrow road loss to BYU.
rationales.Miami: Miami's 9-1 mark includes road wins over Wake Forest and Clemson and a home win over Florida State, though Notre Dame handed it a head-to-head loss.
rationales.Texas: Texas has beaten Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, and its two defeats were both by three points against Oklahoma and Florida.
rationales.Indiana: Indiana's 8-2 FBS record features wins over USC, Michigan, and Nebraska; its recent loss to Washington keeps it below the strongest one-loss resumes.
rationales.Oregon: Oregon's road wins over Ohio State and USC are exceptional, but losses to UCLA, Illinois, and Oklahoma State keep it behind the leading contenders.
rationales.Alabama: Alabama's wins over LSU and Florida State are strong, but losses to Georgia and Tennessee leave it behind teams with better records and comparable schedules.
rationales.UCLA: UCLA's 10-1 record includes an away win over Oregon, and its only loss was a two-point road defeat at Michigan.
rationales.Tennessee: Tennessee's home win over Alabama is a major result, but its losses to Texas and South Carolina temper an otherwise solid 8-2 FBS case.
rationales.Texas Tech: Texas Tech is 9-1 with no one-score losses and wins over Arizona and Houston, though its schedule strength is less imposing than the teams above it.
rationales.BYU: BYU's wins over Notre Dame, Arizona, and Iowa State make a strong case, but its losses to Utah and UCF are meaningful setbacks.
